spec.title: codkit FEAT-003: Requirements for the human working protocol

status.comment: generic human operating protocol for standalone Codkit

p.HP-WRITES-AFTER-FIRST-CYCLE: The protocol (`docs/codkit/protocol/human/*`) is written **after the first manual upgrade cycle on the polygon**: the cycle procedures describe the process that was carried out, not an imaginary one. The protocol does not invent the process — it states a procedure a human can execute on top of the decisions already taken: every requirement refers to a spec and/or a codkit command instead of retelling their behavior.

p.M3-HUMAN-PROTOCOL-IMPL: After the accepted `1.134.0→1.135.0` cycle, `docs/codkit/protocol/human/00-index.md`…`12-maintenance.md`, four shared templates and an executable checker of links, anchors and line caps are implemented. Field tests on new people and the owner-only organizational decisions stay explicitly open and are not marked green.

quality.title: 1. Quality bar (normative for the whole protocol)

facts.HPQ-NUMBERED-PROCEDURES: **Procedures** are numbered steps: the exact codkit command → the expected result (what is printed, the exit code) → the next step; branching happens only on an observable sign («exit 1 and the code `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` → step 4»), never an «act as the situation demands» without a criterion.
facts.HPQ-DECISION-TREES: **Decision trees** have explicit branches and terminal outcomes; every leaf names a layer, a command or an escalation. **Checklists** consist of checkable items (the «yes/no» answer is established by a command or by a look at a concrete output).
facts.HPQ-MECHANIZATION-RULE: **The mechanization rule**: everything a text warns about («do not forget to…») is in fact done by a command, a hook or CI — the protocol refers to the mechanism; a text warning without a mechanism is a defect of the protocol, and a task for the mechanism is opened.
facts.HPQ-SINGLE-DEFINITIONS: The terms follow `common/PROP-003`; one point of definition, everything else refers to it. The language is Russian; the commands and identifiers are English. The clean room is `common/PROP-004`.
facts.HPQ-SELF-CHECK: A self-check of every section before acceptance: «will a person doing this for the first time be able to carry the procedure out without taking a single uncovered decision?» — plus a field test for the key documents (§4).

layout.title: 2. Layout, audiences, sizes
layout.fence: docs/codkit/protocol/human/ 00-index.md the map «who you are → what to read»; the table «norm → mechanism» (§3) 01-quickstart.md the newcomer: onboarding in an hour, three commands, the polygon trainer 02-daily.md the daily discipline of a developer 03-interventions.md editing upstream: the layer decision tree, markers, intervention review 04-team.md team work, conflicts, races, switching branches 05-upgrade-cycle.md the runbook of the upgrade cycle (DRI) 06-history.md the conventions of history and commits 07-upstream-watch.md watching upstream, the forecast, «upstream the seams» 08-release-ci.md release, versions, CI, the air-gapped circuit 09-incidents.md incidents and rollbacks 10-roles.md roles, responsibility, rotation 11-metrics.md the metrics and how to read them 12-maintenance.md maintenance of the protocol templates/ the PR checklist, the cycle issue, the retrospective, the decision journal

facts.HP-AUDIENCES: The audiences: the ordinary developer (hundreds of them; some touch upstream files once a quarter) reads 01 and 02 as a duty and 03/04 as needed; the intervention reviewer — 03, 10 (+11); the upgrade team and the DRI — 05, 06, 07, 09, 10 (+08, 11); the release engineer — 08, 10; the protocol maintainer — 12 and everything else.
facts.HP-SIZE-LIMITS: The size guidelines are a hard upper bound of acceptance (lines): 01 ≤ 150; 02 ≤ 250; 03 ≤ 350; 04 ≤ 200; 05 ≤ 500; 06 ≤ 120; 07 ≤ 200; 08 ≤ 300; 09 ≤ 250; 10 ≤ 200; 11 ≤ 150; 12 ≤ 100. The brevity follows from the rule «refer to the mechanism instead of retelling it».

sections.title: 4. Requirements for the sections (goal / content / acceptance)

facts.HP-ROLES: **10-roles** — the table of roles: the DRI / merge captain of the cycle (appointed per cycle; rights: the cycle branch, running `cycle`, merging), the subsystem owners (the keys of `delta/owners.json` ↔ the inventory; they must react to the addressed notifications of the forecast and to the red list within a working day — a weekly cadence does not tolerate week-long pauses), the intervention reviewers (the right to approve a descent down the hierarchy of layers), the release engineer (`publish`, the supply kit), the upstream watcher, the protocol maintainer. For every role: the duties, the inputs and outputs, the SLA; and the procedure «a rehearsal on draft branches before the first real cycle». Acceptance: for every artifact of the process (a PR, the red list, the journal, a release) the responsible person is defined unambiguously; there is no action without a role.
facts.HP-DAILY: **02-daily** — the formula of the day (word for word in meaning): **the history, the branches and the PRs live in the patch set; editing happens in the fork tree**. The loop: `codkit load` (on a `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE` refusal — `codkit save` first) → an edit in the tree (own code in `src/vs/patchset/**`; upstream files only through 03) → `codkit status` → `codkit save [--commit]` → a commit/PR in the patch set. Plus: how to obtain the tree locally (the resolver, `clone`, `check-tree`); building and running (`build up` → `build errors` once, the output in full; the run is `scripts/code.sh` from the tree; the prohibitions: a direct tsc, `npm run compile` while the daemons are alive, `npm install` without stopping the daemons); what is forbidden in the tree; a multi-root IDE and which Git panel shows what; the PR checklist. Acceptance: after 01 a newcomer carries out the full loop «an own edit + an edit of an upstream file → a PR» on the polygon without questions (a field test on two people who did not take part in the development).
facts.HP-QUICKSTART: **01-quickstart** — within 1 hour: half a page of «how it is built» (the two repositories; the patches as the truth; the picture «patchset → load → tree → save → patchset»); three commands with examples of their output; the «five prohibitions» (a commit into the tree; an edit outside a marker; deletion of upstream lines; a direct compiler; a hand edit of `product.json`); five training assignments on the polygon with a self-check: (a) `load` + running the product; (b) an own edit → `save` → see the diff in the patch set; (c) `marker new` → an edit of an upstream file → `save` → find your own patch and the inventory entry; (d) an edit outside a marker on purpose → read the `save` refusal; (e) a `load` with unextracted work on purpose → read the refusal of the guard. Acceptance: two people «off the street» get through it in ≤ 1 hour.
facts.HP-INTERVENTIONS: **03-interventions** — the layer decision tree (the terminal leaves are a layer + a command): «can it be expressed by own code?» → own; «replace the behavior of a service?» → service-override (check `forbiddenServiceIds`); «remove something upstream?» → hide + a guard test; «JSON without comments?» → config-overlay; «a binary?» → resource-file + a guard; «a uniform mass edit?» → rewrite-rule (agree it with the upgrade team); otherwise → a patch with a marker, and a justification in the PR is mandatory. How to shape a marker (ASCII; the hook goes into `create*`, not into the constructor; DI through an accessor; the logic lives in own; upstream lines are commented out). The intervention review: the questions of the hierarchy; a check of the metadata; the diff of the inventory and the «effective diff» are the subject of the review, the patch files are not; the intervention budget of a subsystem (the thresholds are an open question, §6). De-intrusion iterations: a periodic pass over the patch and rule entries of a subsystem — what to lift into an upper layer, what to upstream as a seam. Acceptance: on five training cases three different people arrive at the same leaf of the tree; the reviewer's checklist covers every check of `verify` without duplicating them in text.
facts.HP-TEAM: **04-team** — procedures by race scenarios (symptom → diagnosis → steps): R1 — a Git conflict on a patch file while merging main: take the version of main → `codkit load` → `codkit reresolve <file>` → `codkit save`; R2b — a red pin guard: merge main → `codkit rebase-onto-pin` → resolve → `save` → push; R4 — a `load` refusal with unextracted work; switching branches: `git switch` → `codkit load` (mandatory, under the guard); `CK-E-LOCKED` — wait for or check somebody else's process. Explicitly: files that do not overlap require no coordination at all. Acceptance: scenario S12 and the R1 case can be walked through from the text of the document by a person who has not seen the architecture specs.
facts.HP-UPGRADE-RUNBOOK: **05-upgrade-cycle** — the DRI runbook: the cadence (weekly; the pin moves only on a green CI; batching is an exception of ≤ 2 tags by a DRI decision); a step-by-step runbook over the phases of `codkit cycle` — for every phase the command, the expected output and code (0/1/3), the control points; the table of outcome classes with the action for each one (shifted/merged — the machine; conflict — a resolution in the tree; target-deleted — an owner decision, and abandoning the intervention = a separate commit that deletes the artifact with an explanation; target-renamed — a check of the automatic port; rule-broken — a repair of the rule; contract-failed — semantic drift, an analysis of the cause; the class «divergence of two upstream branches» is absent from the patch model — this is recorded explicitly); the escalation of design decisions (the signs → a stop, an issue, an owner decision, an entry in the journal); the journal and the retrospective with the metrics; the light procedure of a minor security bump; the templates of the cycle issue and PR. Acceptance: a maintainer who did not take part in the development of codkit walks the polygon cycle `1.134.0→1.135.0` (S08–S10) through from the document alone; every stopping point is recognized; the journal is complete.
facts.HP-HISTORY: **06-history** — the canonical set of the cycle commits and the «do not squash» rule (the cost metric lives in the history); the hook puts the trailers in and CI checks them (the text only explains what for); the authorship of the generated tree commits is a technical author, and their SHAs go into the file of revisions ignored by blame; the history of the patch set is not rewritten; LF/`core.autocrlf=false`/`core.longpaths=true`. Acceptance: three questions are answered from the document without reading the architecture specs: «why the cycle branch cannot be squash-merged», «where Cause comes from», «what blame is to do in the tree».
facts.HP-UPSTREAM-WATCH: **07-upstream-watch** — the role of the watcher (who reads the iteration plans and the release notes of the VS Code team, and where the digest is written); how to read the `codkit forecast` report (a nightly job; addressed notifications to the owners), when to start the adaptation before a release (a conflict class in the forecast → the adaptation does not wait for the cycle); the policy «upstream the seams, not the features»: the criteria of a candidate (a patch that has survived ≥ 2 adaptations; a seam that removes a patch for good), the process of a PR into `microsoft/vscode` (minimal, without our functionality, motivated by extensibility), and the bookkeeping: the patch stays until acceptance and after it the artifact is deleted by a separate commit. Acceptance: from a forecast report with one red intervention an owner determines their actions for the week without questions.
facts.HP-RELEASE-CI: **08-release-ci** — the versioning scheme (the patch set has a version of its own, the pin is a machine field; the exact scheme follows the status of the open choice in PROP-012 §5); `codkit publish` — who (the publish bot only), when, idempotency; air gapped is the main mode: four ways to obtain the tree in CI with the recipes from `docs/codkit/ci-examples/`; the zones of responsibility (the image, the caches — a single writer, the supply kit — who refreshes it on an advisory); the verify/build profiles; what to do on a cold build. Acceptance: a customer's engineer brings a `verify` job up on their own CI from the document and the ci-examples alone (a field test on a «foreign» runner).
facts.HP-INCIDENTS: **09-incidents** — «symptom → steps» procedures with a completion criterion: (a) upstream broke a critical seam (the contract test of the seam is red / the forecast is on fire): an assessment through the cause → an owner decision (rework the intervention / a temporary rollback onto the old pin) → an issue to upstream if needed; (b) a rollback of the cycle: before the merge — `cycle restart`; after the merge — revert commits of the cycle branch (the history is not rewritten) plus a return of the pin in the same canonical format; (c) a hotfix on top of an old pin: a branch from the last release commit of the patch set → an edit under the usual discipline → `publish` with a release tag (the self-consistency invariant makes this a routine); (d) a fast port of an upstream security fix without a full bump: a marker or add-file patch with a cause; it is removed automatically at the next cycle (a regeneration against the new pin, which already carries the fix — «the patch became empty → delete it»). Acceptance: a tabletop game over every scenario on the polygon, with the time recorded.
facts.HP-METRICS: **11-metrics** — which series are written (`inventory-history.csv`): the number of interventions by layer and by subsystem (the target trend falls for the rule and patch layers), the hours per cycle, the time «a VS Code release → our release», the conflicts per cycle, the share of resolutions done by agents, the coverage by contract tests; how to read them (the trend, not the absolute value — the baseline comes from the first cycle); the threshold alerts (the values are an open question, §6); who looks at them and when. A dashboard comes later; until then — a table in the retrospective. Acceptance: from the CSV of two training cycles a person builds the conclusions of the retrospective by the template.
facts.HP-MAINTENANCE: **12-maintenance** — the shared protocol is versioned with toolRoot; a patch set keeps only its own owners, journal and intervention evidence. The shipped `toolRoot/config/conventions.json` is the base machine source; an explicit additive extension in patchesDir adds to it per PROP-003 and never weakens it. Agent and human documents refer to the effective policy; the docs gate checks the paths, the commands and the schema-2 roots.
facts.HP-PRODUCT-NOTE: No separate section about product work is created: work on the features of the product follows the same discipline of layers, markers and review — `00-index.md` carries one paragraph with this norm and a reference to 03.

order.title: 5. The order of writing and acceptance

facts.HPO-ORDER: It is written after the first manual polygon cycle: 05 first (while the traces of the cycle are fresh), then 02/03/04 (following the traces of filling the polygon), then the rest; 01 comes last (the digest).
facts.HPO-FIELD-TESTS: The field tests of acceptance (02, 01, 05, 08) are mandatory and are part of the criterion of milestone M3.
facts.HPO-TEMPLATES: The `templates/` are created together with the document that uses them. Before the commit of every document — the clean-room check and the self-check of §1.

facts.HPOQ-DRI-ROTATION: **The rotation of the DRI**: the term and the order are not decided. Recommendation: a DRI for one cycle, rotation around the upgrade team, and the new DRI assists the previous one for one cycle. **Requires an owner decision** (organizational).
facts.HPOQ-BUDGETS: **The numeric intervention budgets and the threshold alerts**: no values are assigned before the baseline exists. Recommendation: after two cycles the budget = the current value for the subsystem, and the alert is any growth of the rule and patch layers two cycles in a row. Decided by the subsystem owners + the DRI; recorded in 11-metrics.
facts.HPOQ-DEINTRUSION-PERIOD: **The period of de-intrusion iterations**: the recommendation is every fourth cycle; decided together with the budgets.
facts.HPOQ-BATCHING: **The cadence** is decided (weekly) — the protocol does not discuss it, it only executes it; the batching parameter is «no more than two tags, only by a DRI decision» and is recorded in 05.
facts.HPOQ-AGENT-BOUNDARIES: **The boundaries of agent rights** are the subject of FEAT-004; the human protocol only refers to the journal of agent decisions and to the role of the reviewer of agent resolutions.
facts.HPOQ-TREE-HOOK: **The pre-commit hook in the fork tree** — the open choice was closed by an owner decision of 2026-08-31: every `load` tries to restore the owned hook, but the guard counts as active only when Git demonstrably executes its exact current bytes. In an ordinary checkout a manual commit is rejected and the internal path is separated by `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1`; a linked worktree, a custom/global/system `core.hooksPath`, `/dev/null`, a foreign hook or an unresolvable effective path give an explicit warning/false, without a promise of blocking (PROP-012 §5).
